import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('data/dogs_zurich.csv')

# Aggregate the data to get the total number of dogs per district per year
# We sum 'AnzHunde' which represents the number of dogs for each record.
df_agg = df.groupby(['StichtagDatJahr', 'KreisLang'])['AnzHunde'].sum().reset_index()

# Sort the aggregated data by year for correct plotting of time series
df_agg = df_agg.sort_values(by=['StichtagDatJahr', 'KreisLang'])

# Set up the matplotlib figure and axes
plt.figure(figsize=(14, 8))

# Create a line plot to show the trend of dog registrations over time for each district
sns.lineplot(
    data=df_agg,
    x='StichtagDatJahr',
    y='AnzHunde',
    hue='KreisLang',
    marker='o',  # Add markers for each year
    linewidth=1.5,
    palette='tab20' # Use a distinct color palette for districts
)

# Add title and labels for clarity
plt.title('Total Number of Registered Dogs in Zurich by District (2019-2025)', fontsize=16)
plt.xlabel('Year', fontsize=12)
plt.ylabel('Number of Dogs Registered', fontsize=12)

# Customize x-axis ticks to show all years present in the data
plt.xticks(df_agg['StichtagDatJahr'].unique(), rotation=45, ha='right')

# Add a grid for better readability of values
plt.grid(True, linestyle='--', alpha=0.7)

# Place the legend outside the plot area to prevent overlapping with data
plt.legend(title='District', bbox_to_anchor=(1.02, 1), loc='upper left', borderaxespad=0)

# Adjust layout to prevent labels from being cut off
plt.tight_layout(rect=[0, 0, 0.88, 1])

# Save the figure
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
